title: "Dark/Light Vellum Plot"

```{r}
#| include: false
knitr::knit_hooks$set(crop = knitr::hook_pdfcrop)
```

In [my post yesterday about `{vellumplot}`](/posts/2026/08/2026-08-10_vellum/), I mentioned how the default rendering doesn't play nice with Quarto's `renderings[light,dark]` code chunk options, but you can get around it by adding `.light-content` and `.dark-content` css classes to the code chunk.

However, I noticed that the `vellumplot::plot_svg()` function has a `recolor` argument:

> Optional named character vector mapping a **source colour** to a replacement written verbatim into the SVG — e.g. `c(grey30 = "currentColor")` makes a `grey30` sparkline follow the surrounding text colour (dark-mode-adaptive inline).
> Each name is resolved to its hex and swapped for the value; use for CSS keywords (`"currentColor"`) or `var(--x)` that R's colour engine can't emit itself.

So, I wanted to experiment with that.

```{r}
library(vellumplot)
library(purrr)
```

First, I'll set up a plot of the Palmer Penguin data.

```{r}
penguins |> 
  vplot() |> 
  mark_point(
    x = bill_len,
    y = bill_dep,
    color = species
  ) |> 
  scale_color_discrete(
    palette = "Zissou 1"
  ) |> 
  labs(
    title = "Palmer Penguins"
  ) |> 
  theme_minimal() ->
  peng_plot

peng_plot
```

```{r}
#| include: false
vellum::render(
  peng_plot,
  path = "images/peng.png"
)
```

The theme elements are accessible in the plot's `theme` slot.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Plot theme slot

```{r}
peng_plot@theme
```
:::

So I'll grab each named color from the penguins plot.

```{r}
peng_plot@theme |> 
  map(
    safely(
      \(x) x@colour
    )
  ) |> 
  map(
    \(x) x$result
  ) |> 
  keep(
    is.character
  ) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unique() ->
  plot_colors
```

```{r}
#| crop: true
#| out-width: 60%
scales::show_col(plot_colors)
```

Now, it's a matter of figuring out how these specific colors ought to be replaced by some CSS variables.

- `white`: This is the main plot background

<!-- -->

- `black`, `grey10`, `grey30`: These are all colors of text

- `grey92`: This is the panel grid color\

I'm not a CSS whiz, but in digging through the bootstrap themes, I settled on these variables.

- Background: `--bs-body-bg`

- All text: `--bs-body-color`

- Grid color: `--bs-secondary-bg`

For the text colors, there are variables like `--bs-secondary-color`, but I found that they were too faint for text.
Another kind of annoying thing is that even with the darkly bootstrap theme, the default `--bs-secondary-bg` is way too light, and I don't understand CSS enough to get the darker version.

But here it is!
A single code chunk writing an svg string with the colors specified with CSS variables.
If you toggle between light and dark modes, the plot should also update.

```{r}
#| echo: fenced
#| results: asis
peng_plot |> 
  plot_svg(
    recolor = c(
      white  = "var(--bs-body-bg)",
      black  = "var(--bs-body-color)",
      grey10 = "var(--bs-body-color)",
      grey30 = "var(--bs-body-color)",
      grey92 = "var(--bs-secondary-bg)"
    )
  ) |> 
  cat()
```
